title: Rapid slot-leak hunts, rollback runbook, and telemetry hardening for hosted API capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After the Feb 7th hosted API degradation, we observed repeated multi-hour reductions in available inference slots that caused queue buildup and throttling. Root-cause analysis points to a tenant-scoped slot accounting regression in the admission controller where ephemeral preempted slots were not reclaimed under certain failure paths (delta: ~38% effective capacity loss over 3 hours on affected pools). Secondary contributors: an aggressive prefetch path that increased slot hold times for warmups, and KV-cache eviction storms that amplified tail latency and prevented fast reclaim. This ticket designs a rapid hunt/rollback runbook plus telemetry hardening and small code fixes to prevent recurrence.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A tested rollback script that reduces slot leak within 10 minutes in canary; 2) Telemetry shows reclaim events and slot counts per-tenant with 1s resolution; 3) Fix merged that ensures admission controller reclaims preempted slots on all error paths; 4) Load test reproduces prior leak scenario and shows stable capacity for 2h at 1.2x baseline traffic; 5) Runbook published in Confluence and ops trained.
action_items: A. Implement fast rollback script that force-closes leaked slot handles and marks them free in slot DB (owner: Marcus Lee, ETA: 2025-02-14)
B. Patch admission controller to add finally-style reclaim in all early-return/error branches and add unit tests (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2025-02-20)
C. Add per-tenant "leaked_slot_count" gauge and per-pool reclaim histogram to runtime telemetry with 1s granularity (owner: Diego Ramos, ETA: 2025-02-17)
D. Create a non-destructive canary to run rollback script on 1% of traffic and a chaos test to ensure no regression (owner: SRE team, ETA: 2025-02-18)
E. Reduce prefetch warmup hold-time default and add conservative jitter on prefetch admission (owner: Runtime team, ETA: 2025-02-21)
F. Postmortem doc and Confluence runbook with play-by-play troubleshooting checklist and escalation matrix (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2025-02-24)
G. Add alerting: leaked_slot_count > 5% of pool capacity for >5m triggers PagerDuty with suggested mitigation steps (owner: Observability team, ETA: 2025-02-17)
H. Coordinate customer communications for top 10 impacted tenants and offer guidance on retry/backoff recommendations (owner: Customer Success, ETA: 2025-02-19)
